blockers.title: multiComponentSharedLaneSelection is asserted to be inside the custodied ownership record, but both clauses that enumerate the record's membership exclude it and it has no completeness rule, so an absent or weakened predicate silently under-selects SL-2/SL-3/SL-4
blockers.subjectEvidence: The new node carries exactly three fields - standing, predicate, notATriggerTable. Its sibling sharedSurfaceConsumers carries four, the extra one being an explicit completeness rule. The new node has none. Its standing borrows one by reference: 'Same custody digest, completeness, and self-change as unit maps and sharedSurfaceConsumers' - but neither referenced completeness rule is meaningful for a predicate. Unit-map completeness is 'Every first-slice source unit MUST appear exactly once'; consumer completeness is 'Every shared-surface ownerId ... MUST list its consumer set'. Neither says the predicate must exist or what its threshold must be. Meanwhile the two clauses that enumerate what the ownership record contains both omit it. /selector/authority: 'The ownership record is the only impact authority. It includes: unit→owner maps, shared-surface→consumer-component edges, and the previous/current comparison basis' - three items. /selector/algorithm/inputCompleteness: 'Ownership unit maps, sharedSurfaceConsumers, and DR-103 dependency edges are on one closed authority roster. Each has schema/custody, previous/current self-change expansion, and missing/conflicting → AMBIGUOUS' - three items again. Only perLaneExplanation and inputsDigest name the predicate as a member, so the artifact enumerates its own ownership record four times and disagrees with itself two-to-two.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The v4-to-v5 diff confirms /selector/algorithm is on the closed roster and was heavily rewritten - steps, ambiguityPolicy, and the whole output object all moved - while inputCompleteness inside that same opened node was left byte-identical. /selector/authority was not on the roster and so was unreachable, but inputCompleteness was reachable and not amended. This is the same shape as the v3 defect this reviewer recorded as V3-B1: an unmade edit inside a node the successor opened.
blockers.counterexample: Commit an ownership record whose predicate is absent, or whose threshold reads 'cardinality >= 5'. Change bytes under component A, where B declares a dependency on A. Step 2 resolves every changed unit cleanly to one in-universe owner. Step 3 raises nothing: its four AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY conditions are zero owners, out-of-universe ownerId, missing component declaration, and incomplete universe, and none inspects the predicate. The inputCompleteness rule that would have caught it - 'missing/conflicting → AMBIGUOUS' - is scoped to a closed roster of three members that does not include the predicate, so it does not reach. Step 5's fixpoint dutifully repeats 'ownership-record.multiComponentSharedLaneSelection', which contributes nothing because there is nothing there. Selected = {A-lane, B-lane}; cardinality 2. SL-2, SL-3 and SL-4 land in skipped[], and each skippedLaneProof is satisfiable truthfully - it requires attesting that no 'multiComponentSharedLaneSelection ... rule selected it', which is precisely true when the rule is gone. G16-5 does not catch it either: it governs SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 only 'when selected'. No change class forces a predicate mutation beyond the generic C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD, and selfChange expands over unit claims, which a predicate-only edit does not touch.
blockers.impact: The lanes lost are the cross-component protocol, semantic-authority and lock/compatibility gates - OBL-4's entire discharge, and the exact obligation MCICV4-B2 was raised about ('no authoritative multi-component-to-shared-lane selection path'). The repair's whole claim to answer that blocker is the notATriggerTable sentence: 'This is a named predicate inside the custodied ownership record, not a second uncustodied authority.' Custody is what makes that sentence true, and custody here means membership on the inputCompleteness roster with a missing→AMBIGUOUS consequence. Without it the predicate is custodied only by assertion, and an affected omitted lane again has a lawful proof - which the live DR-G16 constraint cell forbids without waiver.
blockers.requiredRepair: Decide which of the two things the predicate is, and say so once. If it is record data: add it to /selector/authority's enumeration and to inputCompleteness's closed authority roster, and give it its own completeness rule - the predicate MUST be present, its threshold is fixed at cardinality >= 2, and absence or alteration is AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY - plus a corpus change class forcing that mutation, alongside C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD. If it is instead a contract-fixed rule that no committed record may vary, then drop the custody framing and state that the predicate is normative in this artifact and not a record field; that also resolves the finding. Either way inputCompleteness must stop claiming a closed roster that excludes a member the same artifact places inside the record.

shouldFix.title: The rewritten ambiguity enum cannot represent a conflict that lawfully resolves to REFUSE, conflating the two classes G16-3 exists to separate
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: Step 3 defines two ambiguity classes and three lawful outcomes: AMBIGUOUS-REFUSE-ONLY always refuses, and 'More than one owner → AMBIGUOUS-CONFLICT (SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE only if the comparison-basis universe is independently complete and valid; otherwise REFUSE).' The rewritten enum offers two ambiguous values: 'ambiguity = none | refuse-only | conflict-universe'. The third lawful outcome - a C-MULTI-OWNER conflict on an incomplete universe, which step 3 and comparisonBasis.law both require to REFUSE - has no value. Emitting 'refuse-only' misreports the class as one of the four REFUSE-only conditions; emitting 'conflict-universe' misreports that universe selection occurred when it did not.
shouldFix.impact: G16-3 is the class that tests exactly this split, and the selectorDecision is the record it inspects. If the record cannot distinguish 'refused because the class is REFUSE-only' from 'conflict that refused because the universe was incomplete', then G16-3's central distinction is unauditable from the emitted evidence, and the repair that produced the split is enforceable only by reading the implementation rather than its output. The field was rewritten at v5 for this exact purpose, so this is an incomplete enumeration in a newly-repaired clause rather than inherited text.

systemicObservation: v5 is the first successor in this chain to fix the process rather than only the findings. It restored the roster catch-all, named every re-measurement block, labelled the historical ones, retracted one of its own earlier false repair claims, and repaired the two blocked-on-ride sites in place instead of adding a third override. Fourteen measurements pass and every one of this reviewer's v4 findings is discharged. The two defects that remain are the same species as before, and both are now detectable mechanically: when a repair adds a member to a set, grep every clause that enumerates that set (V5-B1 - four enumerations of the ownership record, two of which omit the new member); and when a repair adds a required field to an evidence object, grep the acceptance classes for that field's name (V5-S3 - three digest names, zero occurrences in g16Tests). Both checks are cheap, both would have run clean at v4's authoring, and both fail at v5's. Adding them to the authoring pass alongside the abolished-term grep this reviewer proposed at v4 would close the remaining recurrence.
verdictBasis: One blocker and three SHOULD-FIX findings survive; the dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero and zero. All six claimed repairs are real and verified against the subject's bytes, and for the first time this reviewer could also verify the predecessor characterization directly, because the frozen Codex v4 verdict was a permitted input. That verification is what produced V5-S1. The blocker is not a carried finding - it is new, introduced by the v5 repair itself: the multi-component predicate was placed inside the ownership record without being added to either clause that defines the record's membership, and without the completeness rule that makes 'custodied' mean anything.
verdictStatement: v5 is the strongest artifact in this chain by a wide margin. Every Claude v4 finding is discharged, including the blocked-on-ride blocker carried since v3, the whole-candidate merge-base baseline first raised at v2, the composite conflict class, and the stale live-pin locators - and the successor retracts its own earlier false claim about the skipped-lane-proof token rather than leaving it standing. The roster is closed with the catch-all restored, and the live coordinator pin is, for the first time in this chain, actually live at the adopted HEAD. What blocks acceptance is a defect the repair introduced. multiComponentSharedLaneSelection answers MCICV4-B2 by declaring itself 'a named predicate inside the custodied ownership record, not a second uncustodied authority' - but /selector/authority still enumerates the record as three things and omits it, and inputCompleteness still declares a closed authority roster of three members and omits it, so the missing-or-conflicting-is-AMBIGUOUS rule never reaches the predicate and it carries no completeness rule of its own. An ownership record shipped without it selects two component lanes, skips SL-2/SL-3/SL-4, and issues a skipped-lane proof that is true as written. Three SHOULD-FIX findings stand alongside: the codexv4 record states the predecessor had no advisories when it has one, the rewritten ambiguity enum cannot express a conflict that lawfully refuses, and no acceptance class anywhere enforces the changeSetDigest and selectorDecisionDigest bindings the MCICV4-B1 repair introduced. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, chooses no CI vendor, mints no D-096 (A) grant, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
coordinatorNote: The v6 roster needs /selector/authority - which has never been on a roster in this chain and is now the stalest clause in the artifact - plus /g16Tests (already covered in full) and /appliesFindingsOf and /honestyRepairsFromV4 (already covered). /selector/algorithm covers both V5-S2 and the inputCompleteness half of V5-B1. So the only genuinely new path v6 requires is /selector/authority; every other repair above is reachable under a roster shaped like v5's. Two notes on scope. First, V5-B1 admits a one-sentence resolution in either direction - declare the predicate contract-fixed rather than record data, or complete its custody - and the coordinator should pick which, because the two answers have different consequences for whether a committed record may ever vary the threshold. Second, this is the first cycle in which the frozen predecessor Codex verdict was readable under the dispatch, which is what allowed V5-S1 to be found at all; the Claude v3 and v4 verdicts each had to record the Codex characterization as uncertifiable. Keeping frozen predecessor verdicts readable while barring the concurrent reviewer is the right line and is worth preserving explicitly in future prompts.
